stages.overview: One headless host owns the CoreSpace basis, CameraRig, and one SceneEnvironment; application chrome remains outside R3F.
stages.usage: The live canvas mounts one SceneCanvas and configures its environment through the public host API.
stages.variants-states: Home, top, and focus camera modes are exercised with the diagnostic axes enabled on the same host-managed floor and grid.
stages.interaction: The LDS SegmentedControl requests camera mode through the host callback; the renderer does not manufacture camera buttons.
stages.accessibility-motion: The canvas has an accessible name, the current camera state is exposed in DOM, and the static review uses demand rendering with no ambient goal motion.
stages.responsive: Resize the Storybook canvas from wide to 320 CSS px: the host remains one full-width canvas and owns no page layout or inspector chrome.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition proves the same host contract inside the approved LDS viewer composition.

stages.overview: Selectable supplies transient hover and one persistent spatial identifier only; product commands stay outside the renderer.
stages.usage: The live canvas wraps plain WebGL meshes in Selectable and controls hover and selection through the public callbacks.
stages.variants-states: The three visible states are neutral, hover, and persistent selection; no product workflow state is implied.
stages.interaction: Pointer hover and click update the controlled identifier, and the LDS action clears it without creating a renderer-owned button.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas is complemented by DOM hovered and selected summaries; selection has no ambient animation.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the spatial subtree remains inside the host canvas while the DOM summary wraps through LDS Stack rather than inventing a canvas layout.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition forwards the selected identifier into the LDS selection inspector.

stages.overview: AmrRobot is a semantic fallback AMR visual, not a task card, command surface, or asset registry.
stages.usage: The live canvas renders framed RobotEntity input directly through AmrRobot.
stages.variants-states: Idle, live, warning, and error use different spatial material and geometry treatment, with persistent selection shown separately.
stages.interaction: Clicking a robot updates the shared selection contract only.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas has a DOM selected-entity summary; this fallback visual has no autonomous motion in review.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the robot geometry scales with the one host canvas; entity details remain a caller-owned DOM concern.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition combines AMR status with LDS inspector and viewport state.

stages.overview: GoalMarker communicates spatial intent only; a product-owned LDS action must still confirm or commit a goal.
stages.usage: The live canvas renders framed GoalEntity input directly through GoalMarker.
stages.variants-states: Valid, preview, and invalid goals differ through solid, wireframe, and invalid-cross geometry as well as tone.
stages.interaction: Clicking a marker updates persistent selection but does not issue a robot command.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas exposes selected goal identity in DOM; animated is false so reduced-motion behavior is inspectable without a loop.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the marker remains viewport geometry while any confirmation copy or action stays in the LDS composition boundary.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition places a planned goal and an invalid goal in the real viewer scenario.

stages.overview: PathRibbon is passive route geometry by default; route editor workflow and navigation lists are not part of this atom.
stages.usage: The live canvas renders framed PathEntity points directly through PathRibbon with opt-in selection.
stages.variants-states: Actual, executing, planned, and blocked paths differ through route treatment, beacon, and blocked marks as well as tone.
stages.interaction: Selection is enabled explicitly in this review and updates only the shared selected identifier.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas has a DOM selected-route summary; animated is false so the executing beacon is deterministic and reduced-motion-safe.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the ribbon remains spatial geometry inside one canvas; route metadata belongs to the adjacent LDS DOM layer.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition combines actual, executing, planned, and blocked paths in one real scene.

stages.overview: SceneStateMarker is host-driven WebGL lifecycle geometry, not a page-level recovery policy or duplicate application error shell.
stages.usage: The live SceneCanvas receives a public renderState and mounts SceneStateMarker only when that state is non-ready.
stages.variants-states: Ready, loading, empty, and recoverable error are individually inspectable without replacing the host canvas.
stages.interaction: The LDS SegmentedControl changes only review state, while the LDS reset action demonstrates caller-owned recovery policy.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas is paired with the opt-in DOM status overlay and LDS status badge; no ambient motion is required for comprehension.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the marker and its opt-in status overlay remain bounded by the host; page-level layout remains LDS-owned.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--loading-error-empty verifies the same renderer states inside the LDS composition boundary.

stages.overview: GltfModel owns placement, loading, source-convention normalization, and placement lifecycle; product asset registry and workflow remain outside it.
stages.usage: The live canvas loads the actual AMR GLB through GltfModel with an explicit core source convention.
stages.variants-states: The visible load badge records loading-to-ready state for the real asset; lifecycle error and retry behavior are asserted by the focused package tests.
stages.interaction: Clicking the loaded GLB forwards one selected identifier through the shared spatial interaction contract.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas is complemented by DOM load and selection summaries; the asset has no ambient review animation.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the GLB remains inside the one WebGL host while asset metadata and recovery actions remain DOM composition concerns.
stages.scenario: visual-alpha--actual-lds-composition proves the actual asset contract beside LDS viewport and inspector surfaces.

stages.overview: PointCloudLayer is a headless WebGL adapter for one validated LK-core point-cloud snapshot; it owns only adapter-created point geometry and material. ROS transport, TF, PCD parsing, LOD, picking, and product viewer UI remain outside this atom.
stages.usage: The live SceneCanvas receives a caller-retained XYZ/RGB Float32Array snapshot with an explicit frame and point budget.
stages.variants-states: RGB-ready, XYZ-fallback, replacement, empty, over-budget, and frame-mismatch fixtures are directly inspectable; no state creates a DOM or SVG point-cloud substitute.
stages.interaction: The LDS Select changes only Storybook fixture state. PointCloudLayer installs no spatial command, point picking, or renderer-owned DOM action.
stages.accessibility-motion: The named canvas is paired with an LDS description list containing frame, requested/accepted count, and layer eligibility; the static snapshots use demand rendering and no ambient motion.
stages.responsive: At constrained width the point geometry stays inside one SceneCanvas while the LDS summary wraps outside the renderer without creating a second viewer shell.
stages.scenario: lds-3d-scenes-point-cloud-foundation--lds-integration proves the same actual WebGL layer inside the LDS Scene3DFrame composition.
